reproducibility_gaps: Requirement files and backend compatibility tables specify minimums or ranges rather than a complete immutable environment lock.
The representative MNIST example does not select a backend, report a random seed, or constrain deterministic execution.
MNIST is obtained through the runtime dataset loader and is not bundled with an archive checksum in the repository.
The example prints test loss and accuracy but provides no immutable expected values or acceptance thresholds.
The multi-backend test matrix and representative workload were not executed in this bounded checkpoint.
No Atlas-paper relationship is asserted for this general-purpose framework.
notes: R3 is supported by pinned source, backend-specific dependency manifests, installation/test instructions, a complete example and an extensive test surface. R4 is blocked by nonlocked backend environments, absent deterministic controls and the unexecuted boundary.
